title: Expression, purification, and characterization of the innate immune sensor MDA5
author: Joiner, Herrero del Valle, et al.

steps.title: Clone mMDA5Δ646‑663 into pET28a+
steps.instruction: Insert the gene encoding mouse MDA5Δ646‑663 into the pET28a(+) (Novagen) vector in frame with an N‑terminal His6‑tag and a thrombin cleavage site for expression in E. coli. The construct yields the following amino‑acid sequence: .

steps.title: Prepare purification buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare all buffers required for the purification (lysis, wash, elution, Buffer A, Buffer B, SEC buffer) in advance and store them at 4 °C as described in the Materials and Equipment section.

steps.title: Lyse harvested E. coli cells
steps.instruction: Thaw the cell pellet, resuspend in lysis buffer (30 mL per 800 mL original culture or 5 mL per gram of pellet), add one EDTA‑free Protease Inhibitor Cocktail tablet and Salt Active Nuclease (10 µL per 50 mL sample), sonicate 5–8 min (5 s on/10 s off, 200 W ≈40 % power) on ice, centrifuge at 38 000 × g for 1 h at 4 °C, and filter the supernatant through a 0.45 µm filter. Discard the pellet.

substeps.instruction: a. Thaw and resuspend pellet in lysis buffer (30 mL per 800 mL culture or 5 mL per g pellet).
b. Add one EDTA‑free protease inhibitor tablet and 10 µL Salt Active Nuclease per 50 mL.
c. Sonicate 5–8 min (5 s on, 10 s off, 200 W, keep on ice).
d. Centrifuge 38 000 × g, 1 h, 4 °C.
e. Filter supernatant through 0.45 µm filter; discard pellet.

steps.title: Immobilized metal affinity chromatography (IMAC)
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a HisTrap column with >3 column volumes (CV) lysis buffer, load the filtered lysate, wash with 15–20 CV wash buffer until A260/A280 return to baseline, elute with 5–10 CV elution buffer collecting 1 CV fractions, and identify MDA5‑containing fractions by SDS‑PAGE. For gravity‑column alternatives use 3–5 mL 50 % Ni‑NTA slurry and a flow rate of 1–2 mL min⁻¹.

substeps.instruction: a. Equilibrate HisTrap column (>3 CV lysis buffer).
b. Load filtered supernatant; collect flow‑through.
c. Wash 15–20 CV wash buffer; monitor A260/A280 to baseline.
d. Elute with 5–10 CV elution buffer, collecting 1 CV fractions.
e. Analyze fractions by SDS‑PAGE to locate MDA5.
f. (Optional) Use Ni‑NTA agarose gravity column: 3–5 mL 50 % slurry, adjust buffer volumes, flow rate 1–2 mL min⁻¹, binding capacity ~20–40 mg His‑protein per mL resin.

steps.title: Anion exchange chromatography
steps.instruction: Combine IMAC fractions containing MDA5, equilibrate 50 kDa Amicon Ultra filters with lysis buffer and concentrate to ≤3 mL. Desalt using an Econo‑Pac 10DG column (equilibrated with 20 mL Buffer A, load ≤3 mL sample, discard flow‑through, add 4 mL Buffer A and collect eluate). Load 4 mL desalted sample onto a Resource Q column equilibrated with 10 CV Buffer A, wash with 5 CV Buffer A, then elute with a step gradient: 10 % Buffer B (15 CV), 20 % B (60 CV), 40 % B (10 CV), 100 % B (10 CV) at 2 mL min⁻¹. Collect fractions; MDA5 elutes at 10–15 % B. Store column eluate at 4 °C overnight if needed. Alternative strong anion exchangers may be used.

substeps.instruction: a. Combine IMAC fractions containing MDA5.
b. Equilibrate Amicon Ultra 50 kDa filters with lysis buffer; concentrate to ≤3 mL.
c. Desalt:
i. Equilibrate Econo‑Pac 10DG desalting column with 20 mL Buffer A.
ii. Load ≤3 mL protein sample; discard flow‑through.
iii. Add 4 mL Buffer A and collect eluate (desalted MDA5).
d. Anion exchange on Resource Q:
i. Equilibrate with 10 CV Buffer A.
ii. Load 4 mL desalted sample.
iii. Wash 5 CV Buffer A.
iv. Elute with step gradient (10 % B – 15 CV, 20 % B – 60 CV, 40 % B – 10 CV, 100 % B – 10 CV) at 2 mL min⁻¹.
e. Monitor UV at 260 nm (optional) for nucleic‑acid contamination.
f. Pause point: store eluate at 4 °C overnight.
g. (Optional) Use alternative strong anion exchange columns.

steps.title: Size‑exclusion chromatography (SEC)
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a Superdex 200 Increase 10/300 GL column with 1–2 CV SEC buffer. Concentrate SEC‑buffer‑equilibrated MDA5 fractions (using 50 kDa Amicon filters) to ≤500 µL. Load onto the column and elute at 0.75 mL min⁻¹, monitoring A280 (and optionally A260). For larger preparations use a Superdex 200 16/60 column and load up to 3 mL.

substeps.instruction: a. Equilibrate Superdex 200 Increase 10/300 GL with 1–2 CV SEC buffer.
b. Concentrate MDA5 fractions:
i. Equilibrate Amicon Ultra 50 kDa filters with SEC buffer.
ii. Concentrate to ≤500 µL.
c. Load onto SEC column; elute at 0.75 mL min⁻¹.
d. Monitor absorbance at 280 nm (and optionally 260 nm).
e. (Optional) For larger scale, use Superdex 200 16/60, load up to 3 mL.

steps.title: Store purified MDA5
steps.instruction: Pool fractions identified as pure by SDS‑PAGE. Use immediately or keep at 4 °C for 1–2 days. For long‑term storage add glycerol to 5 % (v/v), aliquot, flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C (stable ≥1 year). Before any assay, thawed aliquots should be run through a SEC or desalting column to verify integrity and remove glycerol; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles. If aggregation occurs, increase glycerol to 10–20 %. For ATPase assays, use freshly purified protein.

description: Melanoma Differentiation Associated protein 5 (MDA5) is a retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)-like helicase and one of the main innate immune sensors of cytosolic double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), recognizing dsRNAs longer than 100 base pairs (bp) in length. The IFIH1 gene, encoding MDA5, is a hotspot for natural variants with varied clinical associations, including both increased susceptibility to, and protection against, autoinflammatory disorders. Different mutations in the IFIH1 gene cause disease-related phenotypes through a range of underlying molecular mechanisms.1,2,3 This protocol outlines the expression and purification of recombinant mouse MDA5 (mMDA5), which has higher solubility and higher expression yields compared to the homologous human protein, allowing for expression of MDA5 in Escherichia coli (E. coli) without the need for additional fusion protein tags. In the construct used in this protocol (mMDA5Δ646-663), residues 646–663, which are situated in the flexible L2 surface loop of the helicase 2 insert (Hel2i) domain, are deleted to improve protein solubility without affecting the dsRNA binding, ATPase or interferon signaling activities of MDA5.4,5 This protocol can be used to purify a variety of MDA5 mutants, including both gain- and loss-of-function variants, and to study the biochemical properties underpinning their associated disease phenotypes. The purified protein can be used for in vitro structural and biochemical characterization, and this protocol additionally includes instructions for methods used to study the ATPase activity, RNA-binding, and filament-forming properties of purified MDA5 proteins. To investigate the biochemical properties of purified MDA5, RNA can be transcribed in vitro. RNA synthesis can be performed in advance of protein production and stored at −80°C for future use.
